trial_name: TAME — Mild Hypercapnia or Normocapnia after Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest (2023)
citation: Eastwood GM, Schneider AG, Suzuki S, et al. Mild hypercapnia or normocapnia after out-of-hospital cardiac arrest. N Engl J Med. 2023;389(1):45-57.
trial_type: Investigator-initiated, randomised, multicentre, international, parallel-group clinical trial
one_liner: In comatose OHCA survivors, targeting mild hypercapnia (PaCO2 50–55 mm Hg) for 24 hours did not improve 6-month favourable neurological outcomes or mortality compared to targeting normocapnia.

pico.population: Comatose, mechanically ventilated adult survivors of out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) admitted to ICU within 180 minutes of ROSC.
pico.intervention: Targeted mild hypercapnia (PaCO2 50–55 mm Hg) for 24 hours post-randomisation.
pico.comparison: Targeted normocapnia (PaCO2 35–45 mm Hg) for 24 hours post-randomisation.
pico.outcome: Favourable neurological outcome at 6 months (GOS-E score 5–8).

background.existing_knowledge: Death and disability after OHCA are driven by post-cardiac arrest brain injury, compounded by systemic reperfusion injury and hemodynamic instability. PaCO2 strongly regulates cerebral blood flow and vascular tone.
background.knowledge_gap: Observational data linked hypocapnia to worse outcomes after arrest, but suffered from confounding. Mild hypercapnia augments cerebral perfusion but can increase ICP, acidemia, and arrhythmias; net clinical impact was unknown.
background.hypothesis: Actively targeting mild hypercapnia (PaCO2 50–55 mm Hg) for 24 hours improves early cerebral perfusion and increases the proportion of patients achieving favourable 6-month neurological recovery.

methods.design: Investigator-initiated, randomised, multicentre, international, parallel-group RCT with open-label delivery and blinded outcome assessment.
methods.setting: 63 ICUs across 17 countries; recruitment March 2018 to September 2021.

exclusion: Severe COPD with home oxygen therapy

methods.intervention: Targeted mild hypercapnia (PaCO2 50–55 mm Hg) for 24 hours. Recommended deep sedation (RASS -4), ABGs checked at least q4h (alpha-stat approach), and ETCO2-guided ventilator titrations.
methods.comparison: Targeted normocapnia (PaCO2 35–45 mm Hg) for 24 hours using identical monitoring protocol (alpha-stat, q4h ABGs, ETCO2 guidance).
methods.blinding: Clinicians unblinded; assessors of neurological prognostication (≥96 hours) and 6-month outcomes were blinded; statisticians and authors blinded during analysis.
methods.sample_size_power: 1624 patients required for 90% power to detect an 8% absolute increase in favourable outcome (50% to 58%, two-sided α=0.05); inflated to 1700 for withdrawal. Single interim analysis at 850 enrolments (O'Brien–Fleming boundary, P=0.005).
methods.primary_outcome: Favourable neurological outcome at 6 months, defined as Glasgow Outcome Scale–Extended (GOS-E) score 5–8.
secondary_outcomes: Dichotomised favourable neurological outcome at 6 months using all available data
Health-related quality of life (EQ-VAS) at 6 months

headline_bullets: Targeted mild hypercapnia did not significantly alter 6-month favourable neurological outcome (43.5% vs 44.6%; adjusted RR 0.98, 95% CI 0.87–1.11; P=0.76).
All-cause mortality at 6 months was similar between groups (48.2% vs 45.9%; adjusted RR 1.05, 95% CI 0.94–1.16).
Sensitivity analysis excluding co-enrolment in TTM2 was concordant (44.6% vs 44.7%; adjusted RR 1.00, 95% CI 0.87–1.15).
Clear physiological PaCO2 separation was achieved (mean 49.8±4.7 vs 40.8±4.2 mm Hg), but median time in target range was short (4 vs 7 hours).

outcomes_table.outcome: Dichotomised favourable neurological outcome at 6 months (all data)

outcomes_table.note: Higher scores indicate better perceived health
Preplanned approach for competing risk of death

outcomes_table.outcome: Suspected/confirmed raised ICP requiring normocapnia (ICU days 1–7)

safety: Pneumonia (ICU days 1–7): 40.8% (335/821) in hypercapnia vs 43.1% (358/831) in normocapnia (P=0.35).
Suspected/confirmed raised intracranial pressure necessitating normocapnia: 1.6% (13/829) vs 2.3% (19/839) (P=0.31).

domains.notes: Central randomisation concealed allocation until assignment; TTM2 co-enrolment incorporated as prespecified covariate.
Open-label delivery created scope for co-intervention bias; however, outcome assessors and prognostication (≥96h) were blinded.
1700 randomised; 24 excluded due to consent withdrawal. Primary outcome available for 1548 (6.9% missingness); mortality for 1648 (0.9% missingness). ITT analysis used.
Target PaCO2 achieved in 93.4% (hypercapnia) vs 95.9% (normocapnia); median hours in target were 4 vs 7. Early discontinuation in 8.2% vs 3.0% (pH <7.1 in 12 vs 3). NMB used in 67.7% vs 59.1%.
Well-balanced groups: age 61.2±14.3 vs 61.6±13.3 years, shockable rhythm 70.1% vs 72.5%, median arrest-to-ROSC 26 vs 25 min, initial PaCO2 52.8±17.3 vs 52.5±20.3 mm Hg.

internal_validity.verdict: Internal validity is moderate-to-strong with robust randomisation and blinded outcome assessment, though limited by open-label design, overlap in achieved PaCO2, and differential paralytic use.

domains.notes: Reflects a high-functioning OHCA system (mostly witnessed, high bystander CPR, shockable rhythms). Excluded unwitnessed asystole, severe COPD, hypothermia <30°C, and intracranial bleeding.
Requires frequent ABGs, ETCO2 monitoring, and ventilator titrations in well-resourced ICUs; less generalisable to non-shockable arrests or lower-resource settings.

external_validity.verdict: External validity is moderate for comatose intubated OHCA survivors in advanced ICUs, but limited for non-shockable arrests, unwitnessed events, or severe COPD.

strengths: Definitive sample size (n=1700) across 63 international ICUs.
Blinded assessment of 6-month primary neurological outcome (GOS-E) and prognostication.
Demonstrable physiological separation in PaCO2 (time-weighted mean 49.8 vs 40.8 mm Hg).
Prespecified statistical analysis accounting for trial centres and TTM2 co-enrolment.
limitations: Open-label intervention allowed differential co-interventions (e.g., higher neuromuscular blockade use: 67.7% vs 59.1%).
Randomisation occurred a median ~2.5 hours post-arrest, after baseline PaCO2 was already elevated (~53 mm Hg).
Limited duration spent in target PaCO2 range (median 4 hours in hypercapnia group).
Withdrawal of life-sustaining therapy was clinician-directed.
6.9% missingness for primary outcome (mitigated by multiple imputation and record adjudication).

critical_appraisal.summary: TAME is a high-quality, large-scale international RCT demonstrating that targeting mild hypercapnia after OHCA does not improve 6-month neurological outcomes or survival.
strengths: Clear physiological PaCO2 separation between groups
weaknesses: Short duration spent within exact target PaCO2 window

sections.authors_conclusion: In comatose adults resuscitated after out-of-hospital cardiac arrest, targeted mild hypercapnia did not result in a significantly higher percentage of patients with a favourable neurological outcome at 6 months than targeted normocapnia.

clinical_bottom_line.verdict: Do not routinely target mild hypercapnia post-OHCA. Maintain normocapnia and avoid hypocapnia and extreme hypercapnia.
clinical_bottom_line.applies_to: Comatose mechanically ventilated adult OHCA survivors resuscitated and admitted to ICU.
clinical_bottom_line.does_not_mean: Does not mean hypocapnia is safe; avoiding hypocapnia (<35 mm Hg) remains a critical standard of care.
implementation_caveats: Focus on preventing hypocapnia rather than actively driving PaCO2 above 50 mm Hg.
Deliberate hypercapnia increases sedation and neuromuscular blockade requirements without patient-centred benefit.

controversies.notes: Intervention began median 154 min post-arrest with initial PaCO2 ~53 mm Hg, meaning the early post-ROSC hypoperfusion phase had passed.
Median time within the target PaCO2 range was only 4 hours in the hypercapnia group, with 8.2% early discontinuation due to acidemia.
Higher neuromuscular blocker use in hypercapnia group (67.7% vs 59.1%); withdrawal of life-sustaining therapy was unblinded and clinician-directed.

context_related_trials.relation: Co-enrolment permitted; TAME analysis controlled for TTM2 assignment, confirming consistent neutral outcomes across temperature strategies.
Phase II feasibility RCT that established mild hypercapnia safety but was underpowered for neurological endpoints.

unresolved_questions: Would hypercapnia delivered immediately post-ROSC (pre-hospital or <1 hour post-arrest) alter early reperfusion injury?
Is there a specific subpopulation (e.g., severe hypoxic-ischemic brain injury phenotypes) that benefits from augmented CBF via hypercapnia?

numbers_to_remember: Time-weighted mean PaCO2: 49.8 vs 40.8 mm Hg
quick_recall.one_line_takeaway: Maintain normocapnia and avoid hypocapnia in post-cardiac arrest care; routine targeted mild hypercapnia provides no neurological or survival benefit.
